gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui reads open and modern, with lowercase that stands lofty against its capitals and curves you can see right through. Warnes is the showman, every stroke one gauge; the sans does the quiet work.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-modi: Warnes sprawls out with stretched spacing and strokes that never thicken. Noto Sans Modi sits beneath it with light-filled curves and lowercase close to capital height, so the two settle into an easy, uncluttered rhythm.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mono: Loud, spaced-out and uniform in stroke, Warnes has no sparkle, only constant weight. Noto Sans Mono follows with generously spaced, sturdy lowercase, so a long passage feels steady and unhurried, never cramped.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro reads dense and substantial through the middle of each word, with wide entrances into every letter. Noto Sans Mro keeps a long passage feeling solid and modern, while Warnes sits above it, drawn with one nib.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-newa: Strokes that taper out before they touch, with no swelling or thinning, mark Warnes at once. And Noto Sans Newa keeps a long passage easy to follow, its lowercase bowls large and the e plainly open.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham has wide-open e shapes and weighty lowercase. Over a long passage it stays crisp and modern, while Warnes, with crossbars as thick as its stems, supplies the display swagger above.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and approachable, its lowercase band packed high and its terminals flaring outward like tongs. Warnes, stout as pipe cleaner, contrasts nicely.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Warnes draws every curve without pinching, bold and stretched out. Noto Sans Old Permic follows with rounded, open-sided forms and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, so a longer read stays friendly.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Noto Sans Old Persian reads lofty and light, its open counters letting words breathe into the white space around them. Warnes, outlined in one steady thickness, does its best work large.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Noto Sans Old Sogdian stands nearly capital-high in lowercase. Warnes excels at bold, marker-traced display strokes, while the sans stays crisp and approachable even when text shrinks to its smallest sizes.
